# Exercise G257: Groups Generated by Two Involutions

## Problem Statement

> [!question] Exercise M.1
> Classify groups generated by two elements $x,y$ of order $2$.

## Hints

> [!hint]- Hint 1
> Set $z=xy$ and compute conjugation by $x$.

## Solution

> [!success]- Solution
> Since $y=xz$, the group is generated by $x,z$ with $x^2=1$ and $xzx=z^{-1}$. Every element has a unique possible normal form $z^k$ or $z^k x$. If $z$ has finite order $n$, this is the dihedral group $D_n$ (including the usual degenerate small cases); if $z$ has infinite order, it is the infinite dihedral group $\mathbb Z\rtimes C_2$, with the involution acting by inversion. These exhaust the possibilities. $\square$
